title: Course Info
text:
Course description
The process of spiritual formation is intentionally engaged so that habits developed through theological education form students holistically for ministry.

title: Course Info
text:
Program goals
Calvin Seminary forms graduates who discern, with those they serve, answers to four connected questions — Context, Gospel, Calling, Person. Every ministry situation occurs in a context where the gospel is communicated, where God is calling people to his mission, and where God forms the person and role of a servant leader.

title: Course Info
text:
Learning outcomes

Context: Discern how your history, beliefs, and behaviors shape your ability to love God and others.
Gospel: Describe the basic disciplines of the Christian life and their fruit; describe how identity and character are shaped by coursework and ministry practice.
Calling: Discern ways to encourage individual and communal formation through the classic disciplines.
Person: Practice disciplines that sustain a soft heart and thick skin; develop and sustain a Rhythm of Life with a Formation Group / accountability partner / mentor; articulate how formation habits support servant leadership.

title: Rhythm of Life
text: A realistic plan for living your faith — the processes by which you hope to be formed into the image of Christ for the sake of others. Describe how particular Christian disciplines will be integral to your way of life, with reasons (based on your needs and situation) for your choices. Late Rhythms lose one full grade per day. See the handout “Instructions for developing a personal Rhythm of Life.”

title: Rhythm of Life
text:
Working outline
Use this space to draft. The disciplines you actually practice this term (fasting, prayer, Lectio, Examen, confession, Sabbath) are your best raw material — pull from your Reading Responses.

Where I am now — an honest assessment of your current spiritual condition, needs, tendencies, and life situation.
Where I sense God forming me — the shape of the person you hope to become.
Rhythms — the disciplines/practices you’ll adopt, organized by cadence:

Daily — e.g. Scripture, prayer, Examen
Weekly — e.g. Sabbath, worship, confession
Seasonal / occasional — e.g. fasting, retreat, spiritual direction

Why these — reasons tied to your assessment in (1). This is where the grade lives.
Support & accountability — Formation Group, accountability partner, mentor.

title: Readings & Pacing
text:
Three “don’t get caught” moments

Dec 14’s Nouwen (90 pp) — the largest single reading. Pace ~15 pp/day over the last two weeks.
Practices with lead time — the 24-hr fast (Oct 5), the week-long prayer practice you begin ~Oct 26, and Lectio Divina (Nov 16) must start before class.
Late Reading Responses are never accepted, and the Rhythm of Life loses a full letter grade per day. Dec 16 and Dec 18 are hard walls.

title: Readings & Pacing
text:
Books to have on hand
Required (own): Augustine Confessions (Boulding trans.) · Bonhoeffer Life Together · Foster Celebration of Discipline · Nouwen In the Name of Jesus. Recommended: Calhoun, Spiritual Disciplines Handbook. Everything else (Smith, Willard, Peterson excerpts, Thompson, Athanasius, MLK, DeYoung, etc.) is distributed in class / posted on Canvas.

Drop class-distributed PDFs into a readings/ folder and link them here as you collect them.

text:
Week by week

  
    1
    Mon · Sep 14Integrated Formation for Ministry at CTS
    Orientation
  
  
    Read — none. We meet and get oriented.
    📌 By Sep 16, midnight: post Personal Profile answers to Canvas + submit Personal Profile – Submission to prof.
    📌 By Sep 19: read classmates' Personal Profiles.

    ✍️ Response: an Augustinian theological reflection on a formative life experience.
    👥 Guest: Wendy Fisher (Spiritual Director), 2:30–3:15.

title: Reading Responses
text:
How to choose your 8

Weeks with a practice (2, 3, 5, 7, 10) are richest — lived experience makes for stronger, easier writing. A good default.
Nov 23 (Gratitude) is self-contained and over the break — easy to bank.
Dec 14 offers two in one week — handy, but it’s the heaviest reading week; don’t lean on both as your finale.
Space them out: roughly 2–3 in Sep/Oct, 3 in Nov, 2 in Dec. Don’t stack six in December.
You still must read every week whether or not you write — unannounced quizzes can happen.
